name: Apalik
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: only Ross 1988 comparative subgrouping pages named; no descriptive grammar/phonology of Apalik (Ambul) found

sources.citation: Spencer, Juliann, Sara Van Cott & Bonnie MacKenzie. 2013. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Amio-Gelimi Language Area. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2013-017. Dallas: SIL International. 101 pp. (SIL archives 54624; subject languages include Ambul [apo])
sources.note: Nothing. Appendix A is Amio-Gelimi phonetics (phone charts; one sentence on p. 38 mislabelled 'Ambul' vowel sequences); Appendix C.2 reprints the four Ambul wordlists without stress marks; no stress statement anywhere.

sources.citation: Van Cott, Sara, Juliann Spencer & Bonnie MacKenzie. 2011. A Sociolinguistic Survey of Ambul. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2011-050. Dallas: SIL International. 90 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives 43237)
sources.note: Nothing. Appendix A 'Characteristics of the language', A.1 Phonetics (printed p. 41) gives consonant and vowel phone tables and 26 vowel sequences; A.2 Morphology and A.3 Grammar follow (pp. 41-43); no word on stress, accent or tone (a full-text search for stress/accent/penult/syllable = 0). Appendix C.1 phonetic wordlists (Ayuvet, Melenglo, Asepsep, Ambonge, 190 items) carry no stress marks. Sec. 1.2 names the only earlier work: Hoopert & Wakefield 1980 (grammatical notes from Melenglo, pp. 13-22) and Rath 1979 ms.

sources.citation: Chowning, Ann. 1996. Relations among languages of West New Britain: an assessment of recent theories and evidence. In Ross (ed.), Studies in languages of New Britain and New Ireland 1, Pacific Linguistics C-135:7-62.
sources.note: Nothing. Cites Hoopert & Wakefield's 210-word 'Palik' list (1980:7) and their grammatical examples (1980:14, 20-21) for comparison with Sengseng; no phonology of Palik/Apalik.

sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Nothing for Apalik or any Arawe language. Apalik appears in ex. (4.29), ch. 5 SW New Britain network (pp. 160-167: classification; article vowel harmony, e.g. Apalik ukud 'louse', omon 'bird'), ex. (10.85), wordlist appendix. The only 'stress' hits in the book concern Ali (Verner's-law lenition) and Huon Gulf languages.

sources.note: The only earlier first-hand work on Apalik ('Palik'): 210-item wordlist (p. 7) and grammatical notes gathered at Melenglo village (pp. 13-22) per the 2011 survey and Chowning 1996; SIL survey chapters of this series sometimes include a short phonological note that could mention stress. Nothing else in print could contain a stress statement.
